claude_only.name: Which quantity kind does this value express, and through which governed identifier is that kind resolved?
When two candidate units share a dimension but denote different kinds, what evidence disambiguates the intended kind?
Which quantity kinds are admissible in this property slot, and who has authority to add one?
Is the property in fact a nominal property with no magnitude, and therefore outside this mixin?
What are the dimensional exponents of this quantity over the seven ISQ base quantities?
Which dimensional consistency checks must pass before an addition, comparison or assignment involving this value is accepted?
Does dimension equality alone authorise treating two values as interchangeable in this context?
Is the underlying scale ratio, interval, ordinal or nominal?
Which arithmetic operations must be refused on this scale type, and what is returned instead?
If a conventional reference scale is used, which scale definition and edition applies?
How are ordinal codes that look numeric prevented from entering arithmetic pipelines?
Is the value a count of discrete entities, and what entity type is being counted?
When the unit is absent, how does a consumer distinguish 'no unit was recorded' from 'the unit is one'?
For a fraction or logarithmic quantity, what reference value and base are implied by the unit?
Which code system and code identify the unit, and is that code system case-sensitive?
When a UCUM code, a UN/CEFACT common code and a QUDT IRI are all present, which is authoritative and which are derived?
How is the code system version pinned so the same code resolves identically in five years?
What happens when the unit has no code in any bound code system?
What is the authoritative symbol and full unit name, and which locale variants are held?
Which printing and spelling rules are enforced for this unit, and against which pinned style authority?
Is the display string derived from the code or authored independently, and which prevails on conflict?
Which grammar and conformance level govern parsing of compound unit expressions in this deployment?
Are curly-brace annotations permitted, and are they discarded before semantic comparison?
Are syntactically different but semantically equal expressions treated as equal, and is a canonical form stored?
What is the outcome when an expression fails to parse — rejection, quarantine, or acceptance with a flag?
Which prefix set is admitted, and does it include the prefixes adopted by CGPM in 2022?
Are binary prefixes permitted, and how are they kept distinct from decimal prefixes of the same initial letter?
How are compound prefixes, prefixes on non-metric atoms, and the prefixed base unit kilogram handled?
To which system of units does this unit belong, and is it coherent within that system?
Is the unit SI, accepted for use with the SI, off-system, customary, arbitrary or procedure-defined?
Which unit is used for storage and which for presentation when they differ?
What is the numerical value, and which reference type does it bind to — unit, measurement procedure or reference material?
Is the numerical value real, complex, vector or tensor, and how are components carried and ordered?
Is the value/reference pair enforced as atomic, so that no write path can set one without the other?
Is this value a point, a one-sided bound, an interval, or a ratio of two quantities?
For an interval, are the bounds inclusive, and must both bounds share the same unit?
How is a result below a detection limit or outside the measuring interval encoded so it is not aggregated as a point value?
Which value forms are prohibited in this property slot?
How many significant digits are meaningful, and are trailing zeros preserved through storage and serialisation?
Is this value exact by definition or an approximation subject to rounding?
Which numeric representation is mandated to guarantee lossless round-trip, and what is the behaviour if a consumer cannot honour it?
Which rounding rule applies when the value is scaled, converted or aggregated, and is the rounding recorded?
Are the two units commensurable, and by which test — equal dimension, equal quantity kind, or both?
Does commensurability alone authorise comparison here, or is agreement on quantity kind also required?
How are equality and ordering defined when one or both values carry uncertainty or a comparator?
Which comparisons must be refused outright rather than approximated?
What multiplier and offset convert this unit to the coherent SI unit of its quantity kind?
Does the unit require a non-linear conversion function rather than multiplier and offset?
Is this value a point on the scale or a difference, and which conversion rule therefore applies?
Is the stored value the value as originally reported, or a derivative produced by conversion?
What precision or uncertainty was lost in the conversion, and is the pre-conversion value retained?
Is the conversion reversible without drift, and is a round-trip check required before the result is accepted?
Is the reported uncertainty a standard uncertainty, a combined standard uncertainty or an expanded uncertainty?
For an expanded uncertainty, what coverage factor and coverage probability apply, and how was the factor chosen?
Were the contributing components evaluated by Type A or Type B methods, and is the evidence for Type B components recorded?
Is the uncertainty expressed in the same unit as the value or as a relative quantity, and how is that declared?
What tolerance or specification interval applies to this value, and which authority set it?
Is a conformity decision recorded, and what decision rule and guard band produced it?
How does the record keep tolerance distinct from measurement uncertainty so neither is mistaken for the other?
Which units and value forms are permitted for this quantity slot, and with what binding strength?
What plausibility range, cardinality and requiredness apply, and are they hard constraints or advisory warnings?
What must a consumer do when the unit is unrecognised or a constraint fails — reject, quarantine, or accept with a flag?
Is the validation outcome persisted, and is it re-evaluated when the bound registry release changes?
Under which reference conditions is this value defined, and are those conditions recorded as structured data rather than free text?
For a rate or ratio, what is the denominator — per what entity, per what population, per what period?
Does a contextual qualifier change how the same number and unit must be interpreted, and is a consumer required to fail if it cannot interpret the qualifier?
Is any semantic meaning being carried in a UCUM annotation that a conformant parser will discard?
Was this value measured, computed, estimated, asserted, defaulted or converted?
If computed, from which input quantity values and by which documented method or expression?
Is a metrological traceability claim made, and what documented calibration evidence supports it?
When did the phenomenon the value describes occur or hold, and when was the value observed or ingested?
Are both timestamps RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and is '-00:00' preserved where the local offset is unknown?
Over what interval is the value valid, and does it expire or require refresh?
How is a late-arriving or backfilled value distinguished from a genuine change in the measured quantity?
Which registry release supplied the unit definition in force when this value was created?
Has the unit code since been deprecated, redefined or reclassified, and what is the successor and migration rule?
Are historical values reinterpreted under a new unit definition, or frozen at the version of record?
When a value is corrected, is it amended in place, superseded by a new version, or retracted — and what remains visible?
To which external vocabularies is this unit or quantity kind aligned, and is each mapping exact, broader, narrower or approximate?
Where do the aligned standards conflict, and what resolution has been recorded for this deployment?
Is conformance to a named standard being claimed, and what evidence substantiates the claim?
Which alignments are advisory only and must not be used to drive automated conversion?
Which profile and unit value set bind this quantity slot in this exchange, and at what binding strength?
How was the binding agreed with the exchange partner, and where is that agreement recorded?
What is the receiver's behaviour when a value arrives outside the bound value set or violates the profile?
Is the quantity embedded as a value object in the host record, or referenced by identifier, and what justifies the choice?
Which fields are mandatory in every embedding, and which are conditionally required by scale type or origin?
Does the embedded quantity inherit the host record's identity, versioning and audit trail, or does it carry its own?
Which host-model responsibilities are explicitly delegated so this mixin does not restate them?
Can this numeric value, alone or combined with others, re-identify a person or reveal a controlled attribute?
Which access rule applies to the numeric value as against its unit and quantity-kind metadata?
Under which retention rule is the value deleted, and is the unit and provenance metadata retained so remaining data stays interpretable?
Is precision reduction, banding or perturbation applied as a disclosure control, and is that transformation recorded as provenance?

grok_only.name: What quantity is being expressed, as a property of which phenomenon, body, substance, object or event, and is it a particular quantity or only a kind?
If this quantity instance must be cited independently of its host record, what master identifier, governed IRI or Dimension-assigned UUID identifies it?
Which host entity, observation or event embeds this quantity, and is the quantity a measured result, a specified requirement, a constant or a derived calculated value?
Is the quantity treated as a real scalar magnitude, or does the host need vector, tensor or complex structure that this mixin cannot carry alone?
Which quantity kind applies, identified by ISQ name, QUDT QuantityKind IRI, or another governed kind code?
Is this kind a base quantity kind of the governing system of quantities, or a derived kind defined by an equation among kinds?
If other kinds share this dimension, what distinguishes this kind so that conversion or comparison with those kinds is refused?
Which units are applicable to this kind, and which system of units supplies the preferred unit?
What is the dimension vector of this quantity kind in the governing system, including exponents for L, M, T, I, Θ, N and J and any extra base such as angle?
Is this a quantity of dimension one, and if so is an explicit unit still required by SI guidance rather than leaving the unit blank?
Which system of dimensions is the vector expressed in, and is a mapping required because UCUM uses gram, radian and coulomb bases that are not isomorphic with the SI?
Against which other quantities must dimensional homogeneity be proven before addition, subtraction or equality comparison?
Which system of quantities governs this record, and which base quantity kinds does that system declare?
Which defining equations or physical relations of the system are needed to derive this kind from the bases?
Which system of units is explicitly coupled to this system of quantities, and does it define a unit for every kind in use?
What scale type applies to this quantity kind and unit pairing: ratio, interval, logarithmic, ordinal, enumeration or nominal?
Which operations are permitted on values of this scale: addition, subtraction, multiplication by a scalar, ratio, logarithm, or only order comparison?
If the unit is special, what forward and inverse functions convert between the special unit and its corresponding proper unit, including any scale factor from a prefix?
What is the authoritative master identifier of this unit, and which additional coded identities (UCUM case-sensitive, UCUM case-insensitive, UNECE Rec 20, IEC 61360, QUDT IRI) are bound to it?
What print name and print symbol should humans see, and is that display form allowed to differ from the machine code without changing meaning?
Is the unit atom metric, so that an SI or UCUM prefix may attach, and is the atom itself prefix-free?
Which organisation and which version of which specification currently defines this unit, and has the definition been deprecated or replaced?
In the named system of units, is this unit a base unit, a coherent derived unit, a non-coherent derived unit, or merely allowed for use?
If this is an SI base unit, which defining constant and exact numerical value fix it after 20 May 2019?
What is the definitional expression of this unit as a product of powers of the system's base units, including any numeric factor?
Which prefix, if any, is applied, what is its exact scalar value, and is it a decimal SI prefix or a binary information prefix?
Is prefixing legal on this atom, and has a double prefix or a prefix on a non-metric atom been rejected?
Which prefix set version is in force, and does it include ronna, quetta, ronto and quecto or only the UCUM 2.2 yotta-to-yocto set?
If the unit is an information unit, must IEC binary prefixes be used instead of SI decimal prefixes to avoid kilo versus kibi ambiguity?
Is this unit a special non-ratio unit, and what corresponding proper unit and conversion functions apply?
Is the recorded value a level on the special scale, or a difference/interval that must use offset-free conversion?
If a prefix is attached to a special unit, what scale factor divides the function output so that milli-degree Celsius is not treated as 0.001 times a Celsius temperature?
If the value is a count, what is being counted, and is a UCUM annotation or a dimensionless unit one being used as a non-semantic label?
If the unit is logarithmic, what is the reference quantity and logarithmic base, and is the value a ratio of two quantities of the same kind?
Which system or systems of units is this unit a member of, and in each system is it base, defined, coherent, derived or only allowed?
If the unit is outside the SI, is it accepted for use with the SI, tolerated in a named domain, or disallowed by Dimension policy?
If the unit is customary, which national or sectoral variant applies, such as US gallon versus Imperial gallon or avoirdupois versus troy mass?
What numerical value is recorded in the stated unit, and what precision or significant-digit count is implied by its lexical representation?
Was this number rounded, and if it was produced by conversion, what rounding rule from NIST SP 811 or Dimension policy was applied?
At what event time was the quantity true of the world, and at what observation or ingestion time was this numerical value recorded?
What coded unit, coding system URI and human-readable unit are bound to this value, and do they satisfy the rule that a code requires a system?
If a coded unit is missing, is the value unusable for conversion, and is a free-text unit or a dimensionless default of one being used?
Which unit coding system is required in this context of use, and is a translation from a local or trade code still pending?
Is the stated numerical value exact, or is it an inequality relative to a detection or reporting limit, and which comparator applies?
How must comparison, sorting and statistical aggregation treat this censored value so that it is not processed as an exact point?
Which instrument, method or laboratory defined the detection or quantitation limit that produced this comparator?
If the quantity is a range, what are the inclusive low and high limits, in which units, and are the limits commensurable and ordered?
If the quantity is a ratio, what are the numerator and denominator quantities, and why can they not be expressed as a single compound unit?
Is either bound missing, meaning unknown rather than infinite, and how should membership tests treat an open bound?
For this dimension-one quantity, which explicit unit is recorded (one, percent, radian, mole per mole, or another coherent ratio), and is a blank unit forbidden by policy?
If a parts-per-N or percent notation is used, is it a mass ratio, volume ratio or amount-of-substance ratio, and has a deprecated ppb or ppt token been replaced by a power of ten?
Is plane or solid angle being treated as SI dimension one or as a UCUM independent dimension, and which convention must receivers use for commensurability tests?
Do two unit expressions denote the same unit under the governing semantics, even if their literal codes differ?
Are the two units commensurable, and if so what is the relative magnitude of the first regarding the second?
Is the engine operating in full semantic conformance or limited literal conformance, and which expressions will therefore be missed as equivalents?
Does a quantity-kind mismatch block conversion even though the dimension vectors match?
What conversion multiplier and offset map this unit to the named reference unit, and is the mapping exact or experimental?
What canonical or reporting unit does Dimension policy require, and must the original unit and original numerical value be stored alongside the converted value?
After conversion, how many significant digits are kept, and was rounding applied in the direction required by the receiving process?
What algebraic operation is requested among which operand quantities, and is each operand dimensionally legal for that operation?
What quantity kind, dimension and coherent unit does the result have, and must the numerical value be recomputed in a coherent system to avoid hidden factors?
If a non-coherent unit such as hour or millimetre appears in a product, how are prefix and conversion factors accumulated so that the numerical-value equation stays correct?
Is this quantity a delta or interval rather than an absolute level of the same kind?
Which conversion rule applies: linear multiplier only, or affine multiplier-plus-offset?
If both a level and a delta of the same property exist, how are they related, and may they share a unit symbol that differs only by interpretation?
What standard, combined and expanded uncertainties are attached to this quantity value, in which unit, and with which coverage factor and coverage probability?
Was the uncertainty obtained by Type A statistical evaluation, Type B evaluation, or a combination, and which measurement model version was used?
If uncertainty is absent, is that because the value is a specified requirement rather than a measurement, or is it a quality gap that blocks a decision?
If this quantity is an input to a derived quantity, how must its uncertainty be propagated, and are input quantities correlated?
To which international reference is this quantity value or unit claimed to be traceable, and is the calibration chain documented end to end?
What evidence artefacts support the traceability claim, such as a calibration certificate identifier, mise en pratique citation, or mapping table version?
Which organisation is responsible for maintaining the traceability claim, and under which accreditation or metrological authority?
Where does the chain stop, and is the result therefore only internally consistent rather than metrologically traceable?
Is the unit expression a valid UCUM main-term under the published grammar, and is it case-sensitive or case-insensitive?
What annotation, if any, is present in curly braces, and has it been stripped before semantic comparison?
Which UCUM version and which terminal-symbol table revision define this expression, and would a later prefix or atom change the parse?
What UNECE Recommendation 20 common code identifies this unit in trade messages, and in which quantity category annex is it listed?
What UCUM expression, if any, is the declared equivalent of this Rec 20 code, and is the mapping one-to-one or many-to-one?
Which revision of the Recommendation 20 code list is in force for this message, and has the code been added, renamed or withdrawn?
What QUDT unit IRI and quantity-kind IRI identify this concept, and which vocabulary graph version was used?
Which UCUM, UNECE, IEC 61360 and OM identifiers does the QUDT resource assert, and are any of those assertions missing or conflicting?
Is the QUDT resource a CurrencyUnit or otherwise out of this mixin's physical-quantity scope?
Which source vocabulary concept is mapped to which target vocabulary concept, with what mapping type (equivalent, broader, incommensurable, kind-mismatch)?
What conflict or non-isomorphism applies to this pair, and is automatic conversion therefore refused?
What language-specific unit names are bound to this concept, and which language is authoritative for print?
Who authorised this mapping, under which ISO 11240 or Dimension rule, and at what version?
Which organisation is the master authority for this unit or conversion factor, and which specification URL and version are in force?
What is the effective event time of this definition in the world, and what is the observation or ingestion time into this Dimension?
Is the unit or mapping active, deprecated, withdrawn, or superseded, and what identifier replaces it?
Who is the Dimension owner or maintainer accountable for adopting this definition, and who may approve local aliases?
Which unit codes and systems are allowed, preferred or forbidden in this context of use?
If an inbound unit is unknown or unmapped, is the value rejected, stored as free text without conversion, or queued for stewardship?
Does this context require SI units, SI-accepted units, or permit customary units with mandatory dual reporting?
Who may read versus change the allowed-units policy, and which audit events are required when the list changes?
What original numerical value, original unit, conversion version and conversion time must be retained, and for how long relative to the host record?
Under what conditions may a quantity value be deleted or redacted, and is the unit definition itself never deleted, only deprecated?
Which access scope applies to this quantity value, conversion table or uncertainty statement, and what exception allows an agent to read conversion factors without reading host personal data?
What audit record is written when a value is converted, a factor table is patched, or an original value is redacted?
Does AGENTS.md declare Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL for WM-XCT-008?
In what order must an agent read AGENTS.md, the specification, the allowed-units policy and the conversion table before writing a quantity value?
Which storage type and interface project this mixin, and are agents forbidden from treating that projection as the semantic model?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
